adds.title: The first but not the last: Indonesian transgender man fights for recognition | UNAIDS
adds.summary: Dimas Cahya, a transgender man from Medan (North Sumatra's capital), described to UNAIDS how he became the first transgender man in Medan to legally change his name to match his identity: after a six-week process the Medan District Court granted the application, and the judge, though warning the change would 'erase my identity', stayed out of LGBTI issues completely. The article frames Medan as conservative, with LGBTI people deemed 'immoral', and reports that a Medan legal-aid organisation asked the couple invasive questions before the case. For this record it is North Sumatra's only documented legal-process data point: a local court handled a trans person's application neutrally and no enforcement action against the couple is recorded anywhere in the article.

adds.title: LGBT Manado Aksi Tolak Kekerasan Seksual - SuaraKita
adds.summary: On 11 June 2016 LGBT groups joined Manado's women's movement in a street action against sexual violence at Bundaran Zero Point, Manado, from 08.00 to 10.00 WITA; SALUT (Sanubari Sulawesi Utara), the local LGBT organisation whose director Coco Jericho was quoted, took part. The article records that police raids in Manado have included harassment of LGBT people - a butch lesbian groped during a raid, per SALUT - and that victims often do not report because of fear their families will not accept their orientation. It documents a public LGBT+ presence in Manado and a local account of raid-era conduct, with no arrests or prosecutions reported in the piece.

adds.title: Ketika Waria Berkontes Ratu Pantai - SuaraKita
adds.summary: On Saturday 10 November (2012) a waria beach-queen pageant was held at Malalayang beach, Manado, organised by Indonesian parliament member Paula Sinjal together with the National Narcotics Agency of North Sulawesi (BNN) as an outreach event on the dangers of drugs and HIV/AIDS. The report quotes Sinjal saying waria are among local people and deserve attention. It documents official-level engagement with North Sulawesi's waria community through a public pageant - evidence of a visible, organised trans community in Manado - with no adverse official action recorded.

adds.title: Hari Paling Buruk Dalam Hidup Ratu Waria: Media yang Sensasional telah Hancurkan Hidupku - Konde.co
adds.summary: This Konde.co interview profiles Alexa, elected Ratu Waria Sulawesi Utara 2016-2018 at the Sahid Kawanua Hotel in Manado, who says that after her title she suffered discrimination from sensationalist media and the public, with her personal crisis peaking around 25 March 2019. The article confirms a visible trans-women community culture in North Sulawesi - an elected province-level waria queen in Manado - while documenting the media-stoked stigma that follows public visibility. No legal or police action appears anywhere in the account.

adds.title: POTRET KEHIDUPAN GAY DI KOTA KENDARI | Jurnal Budaya Etnika (ISBI)
adds.summary: A qualitative study by Universitas Halu Oleo researchers, published in Jurnal Budaya Etnika Vol. 8 No. 2 (23 December 2024), describes gay life in Kendari, the capital of Southeast Sulawesi: gay groups in the city say same-sex orientation has partly been converted into an economically valued 'profession', and that after identifying as gay they become more introverted and careful about expressing their feelings to others. The study documents same-sex communities in Kendari living discreetly, with no enforcement incident, raid or local regulation reported in the article. For this record it is the only Southeast Sulawesi-specific community evidence found, and it does not alter the national-framework risk profile described in the record.
